USG:

Thermal effect.

Mechanical effect.

Tissue damage by these (2) effects, in Doppler, in B – mode.

Cavitation:

Inertial – transient.

Non inertial – stable.

More effect if exposure exceeds 60 min.

MRI:

Challenging in obstetrics – to perform and interpret due to fetal movements, MRI better than USG, Safe at any Gestation.

Gadolinium contrast:

Improve imaging – crosses placenta and fetal circulation and excreted in amniotic fluid => risk of fibrosis in nephrogenic system (not) statistically significant.

Risk of SB and neonatal death.

Risk of rheumatological, inflammatory skin diseases.

Avoid – Gadolinium in pregnancy.

Nuclear imaging:

Thyroid scan, bone scan, Renal scan, V/P scan.

Most commonly use “isotope – tech 99)

Gamma rays emitted t/2 = 6 hours.

“rad iodine 13” t/2 = 8 days.

Cause fetal hypothyroidism in 10 – 12 weeks.

“F – FDG” in PET CT.

Avoid – Rad Iodine in pregnancy

Tech 99 & F – FDG can be used => in thyroid scan use Tech 99 in place of radio Iodine.
